name: highlight (Andre Simon)
description: Long-standing C++/Lua highlight-first CLI and library with many output formats (HTML, LaTeX, RTF, ODT, SVG, ANSI, BBCode, Pango)

host-language.comment: Engine and CLI are C++ (Boost headers + Lua 5.x/LuaJIT at build time). Lua is first-class: all language definitions, themes and plug-ins are Lua scripts run by the embedded Lua interpreter.

form-factor.comment: Primarily a CLI (plus optional Qt GUI). The highlight::CodeGenerator class (src/include/codegenerator.h) is the library interface, wrapped via SWIG; a shared library build exists (fixed in 4.22) but the C++ API is not documented beyond the header.

license.comment: GNU GPLv3 per the GitLab project licence (COPYING). Separate licences for individual bundled definitions/themes were not checked.

repository.comment: Hosted on GitLab (project created 2018-06-04; history predates the GitLab move).

package.comment: Official download page is andre-simon.de, which could not be fetched on 2026-11-18 (expired TLS certificate). Debian sid package shown as the primary distro package; note it lags upstream (4.10 vs 4.22).

documentation.comment: The README.adoc manual (also published on andre-simon.de) plus README_PLUGINS, README_LSP_CLIENT, README_REGEX, README_LANGLIST and a man page.

first-release.comment: Predecessor src2css 0.1 released 2002-04-04; renamed highlight 0.1 on 2002-07-25; 1.0 on 2002-08-13.

engine-model.comment: Lua language definitions declare keyword lists/regexes, comments, strings, operators etc.; the C++ parser runs them as a regex state machine with an OnStateChange hook. Optional LSP client can add semantic tokens from an external language server.

regex-engine.comment: Strictly Boost.Xpressive (dynamic sregex::compile), not Boost.Regex; closest available tag. Xpressive replaced highlight's own Pattern/Matcher classes in 3.11 (2012); README_REGEX is based on the Boost regex syntax docs.

embedded-languages.comment: Via NestedSections in language definitions: html.lang embeds CSS (<style>), JavaScript (<script>), PHP and JSP out of the box.

language-auto-detection.comment: Detection is by extension, filename, or first-line 'Shebang' regexes in filetypes.conf (incl. an XML declaration pattern); no general content-based guessing.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: filetypes.conf maps extensions, full filenames and shebang regexes to languages; user-overridable. Ambiguous extensions take the first association in the CLI.

resumable-line-state.comment: Parser state is held in private CodeGenerator members; no public API to save/restore per-line state.

semantic-distinctions.comment: The built-in engine is a regex state machine. Since 4.0 an optional LSP client (--ls-semantic) can apply semantic tokens from an external language server (clangd, rust-analyzer, gopls...), but that requires a separate toolchain and is not built in.

bundled-languages.comment: Count of .lang files in langDefs/ on master (267 via paginated GitLab tree API, checked 2026-11-18, ~4.22). README_LANGLIST lists roughly 255 rows (may lag); some definitions are dialect variants.

grammar-format.comment: Language definitions are Lua scripts (.lang) declaring keywords, regexes, delimiters and optional Lua hook functions (since 3.0, 2010).

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Consumes only its own Lua .lang definitions; no TextMate, Sublime, tree-sitter, Pygments or KDE import.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: Definitions are interpreted at runtime: --syntax accepts a .lang file path, user config dirs override bundled files, plug-ins modify definitions, and CodeGenerator::loadLanguage(path) loads one in the library.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: Only the selected .lang script (plus any nested-section languages) is loaded via loadLanguage(); definitions are separate files on disk, not compiled in.

grammar-accuracy.comment: Judgement call: hand-maintained regex definitions not tracking an upstream grammar. Recent changelog entries fix e.g. Python interpolation outside strings, nested command substitution in shell, Vue nested sections and regexes in CMake/PHP, indicating solid common-case coverage with gaps on nested/modern constructs. No systematic spot check of TS/Rust/Python.

bundled-themes.comment: 97 .theme files in themes/ plus 105 in themes/base16/ (selected as base16/<name>), on master checked 2026-11-18.

theme-format.comment: Themes are Lua .theme scripts (Colour, Bold, Italic, Underline, AnsiIndex, Custom per element). The bundled Base16 collection is pre-converted to .theme files; Base16 YAML is not consumed directly.

token-classification.comment: Fixed element set (Default, Number, String, Escape, Comment, Preprocessor, Operator, Line number, keyword groups 1-n, plus LSP semantic styles); HTML classes like hl kwa/hl str.

css-class-output.comment: HTML/LaTeX/TeX/SVG reference an external stylesheet by default; --include-style embeds it, --inline-css switches to inline styles.

multi-theme-output.comment: Class names are theme-independent, so per-theme stylesheets generated with --print-style can be swapped manually, but there is no documented single-render light/dark mechanism.

public-token-api.comment: CodeGenerator's public generate* methods return only rendered output; token state is private. The Lua Decorate(token, state, kwGroupID, lineHasStmt, lineno, column) plug-in hook sees each token during rendering, but is not a token-stream API.

ir-kinds.comment: No documented intermediate representation; output is always a rendered format.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: No token output; theme colours are only applied inside the format generators.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: No IR. (The Decorate plug-in hook does receive line number and column, since 3.60.)

custom-formatter-api.comment: Output generators are C++ subclasses of CodeGenerator created via an internal factory (getInstance(OutputType)); no documented way to add a new format. Lua plug-ins (Decorate, Header/FooterInjection) can only alter tokens/markup within existing formats.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: Documented Lua plug-in hooks Decorate, DecorateLineBegin and DecorateLineEnd; bundled plug-ins include mark_lines.lua, outhtml_focus.lua, outhtml_codefold.lua and tooltip/link decorators. Applied during rendering (no separate IR).

output-formats.comment: --out-format: html (HTML5, default), xhtml, tex (plain TeX), latex, rtf, odt (Flat XML), svg, bbcode, pango, ansi, xterm256, truecolor. Plain TeX and XHTML have no dedicated tag. No image output.

streaming-output.comment: Reads stdin/files and writes stdout, but no documented incremental output API. --service-mode keeps the process alive for repeated inputs separated by an EOF character, each processed whole.

terminal-ready.comment: ansi, xterm256 and truecolor output formats; README shows `highlight --out-format=xterm256 file | less -R`.

native-dependencies.comment: Native C++ program linking the Lua 5.x (or LuaJIT) runtime; Boost headers (Xpressive) at build time; Qt5 only for the optional GUI.

runs-in-browser.comment: Native CLI/library; no browser build documented.

wasm-build.comment: No official WASM build found in the repository or manual (checked 2026-11-18).

synchronous-api.comment: CodeGenerator::generateString/generateFile are blocking calls after initTheme/loadLanguage. With LSP features enabled, calls wait on the external language server.

bindings-ports.comment: Official SWIG interface (extras/swig/highlight.i) wrapping CodeGenerator, with makefile targets for Python, Perl and PHP; also a TCL extension in extras/tcl. Perl and TCL have no tag.

core-package-size.comment: Native CLI, not comparable with JS/Python package sizes. For reference the Debian sid amd64 binary package installs ~1.45 MB (plus highlight-common data).

throughput-tier.comment: No independent or reproducible cross-engine benchmark including highlight was found in this pass.

initialization-cost.comment: No cited measurement of time-to-first-highlight. Each run starts a Lua state and loads one language and theme script; unmeasured.

github-stars.comment: Not on GitHub. GitLab shows 130 stars and 169 forks (checked 2026-11-18).

monthly-downloads.comment: CLI distributed via source tarballs and distro packages; no single registry with download counts.

maintenance-status.comment: Roughly quarterly releases (4.18 Nov 2025 through 4.22 Nov 2026) with new language definitions, features and issue-linked fixes; last activity 2026-11-15.

documentation-quality.comment: Thorough CLI manual with examples, separate plug-in, LSP, regex, language-list and v4 migration guides; but no API reference for the C++ library beyond header comments.

notable-users.value: ranger file manager (scope.sh previews), fzf.vim preview script
notable-users.comment: ranger's default scope.sh calls `highlight --out-format=xterm256|ansi` first, falling back to bat/pygmentize; fzf.vim's preview fallback runs `highlight -O ansi -l`.

bus-factor.comment: Developed and maintained by André Simon; AUTHORS lists contributed language definitions and bundled third-party libs (Diluculum, astyle, PicoJSON).
